text: Setting clear goals at the start of a project is essential for success. A useful method is to create SMART goals, which means they are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. This helps avoid vague targets and keeps the team focused. Once you have your main goal, break the project down into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that let you monitor progress and celebrate small wins along the way. Each milestone should lead to clear deliverables, such as reports or prototypes. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. This means regularly communicating with everyone involved to confirm that your goals match their expectations. When all parties are on the same page, the project has a much higher chance of staying on track and finishing successfully.
